statement: Let $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 2}$ and $g(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 5}$. Which of the following describes the domain of the composite function $g(f(x))$?

choices.misconception: I kept only the square root restriction from $f$ and thought the composition removed the restriction from $g$, so I excluded nothing else.
I copied the restriction $x \ne 5$ straight from $g$, but in $g(f(x))$ it is $f(x)$, not $x$, that cannot equal $5$.
I saw that $\sqrt{x - 2}$ cannot equal $5$, but I solved $\sqrt{x - 2} = 5$ as $x - 2 = 5$ without squaring the $5$, so I excluded $x = 7$.

hints: Write out $g(f(x))$ as a single expression first.
Two things can go wrong: the square root needs a nonnegative input, and the denominator $\sqrt{x - 2} - 5$ cannot be $0$. Handle each one.

solutions.reliable: $g(f(x)) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x - 2} - 5}$. The square root needs $x - 2 \ge 0$, so $x \ge 2$. The denominator is $0$ when $\sqrt{x - 2} = 5$, that is $x - 2 = 25$, so $x = 27$. Every other $x \ge 2$ works, so the domain is all real $x \ge 2$ except $x = 27$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
